item.title: SCP-5523:
item.content:encoded:
I love how this is essentially a completely natural phenomenon that's anomalous only because the Foundation noticed it somehow. (Well, the fast decomposition is definitely anomalous, that's not what I'm getting at here.) If humans hadn't gotten caught up in this by mistake, it would have just kept right on going and everything would be fine.

That said… It's weird, because once we get to the dead deer sprouting deer food, I totally get it. And yet, this feels like it's too short? I was kind of expecting a much longer article. Maybe it's the brevity of Rothenberger's note, but even that's fine because you prime us with information about what happened to him at the start of the article.

Well, it definitely works, so +1 from me. I also fixed a few things for ya.

item.title: SCP-5179:
item.content:encoded:
I wanted to love this, so, so badly. In truth, I really like this concept, and the disjointed aspect of the white boxes sort of peering into… "someone's (???)" inner life in this town of Astra was fun, albeit a bit off-toned.

However, unfortunately, there's just a massive level of "clutter" that can't be ignored (not even when it comes to the formatting.) The ending is also a bit… flat? Like, I can sort of see what you're attempting with it, but frankly the characters are somewhat baseless that its hard to keep track. It kind of reads like a "trying-to-remember" dream sequence, which may be intentional, but for myself personally it's hard to associate.

I really want to love this, and I see some potential. I'd love to see this rewritten and reworked, since it's just conceptually pleasing for me personally.

EDIT: Should also mention that I like the fourth-wall break (I'm always a sucker for them), but after re-reading, this time it feels entirely off-base from everything else, not to mention gimmicky at best.

item.title: SCP-5510:
item.content:encoded: The whole premise of the article is a clever joke, you can look at some of the other comment after and before this to show how many people find it as a joke. It’s basically the researcher pausing time forever because he was testing an SCP. Also not all Joke SCPs have to particularly funny but instead are clever but don’t meet the standard format for regular pages. As a site moderator I assume you know some of this or have an different opinion but I’ve been on this site for awhile before I got an account and this is the usual trend when it comes to these SCPs. If you have your own explanation for why is should not be a -J please explain.

item.title: SCP-5179: Good Concept, Poor Execution
item.content:encoded: It's a cool idea albeit executed poorly, there is a lot of typos and grammar errors that need to be addressed and the weird white boxes make the page cluttered and difficult to read as you're constantly switching between the two parts of the article. The whole 'Youth passes as a fleeting river, star lies in the silver flower.' is quite a good addition and the fact it addresses the reader is a brilliant touch. Overall, a good concept executed and worded poorly.

item.title: Resurrection:
item.content:encoded:
Just get several of the established Resurrection writers to approve it (you can find us in chat), and you can add once you're done.

Does this not defeat the whole point of a canon?
To me, the fact that neither of the cancon teams have been able to add their series to the hub thus far, even though the contest has ended weeks ago, shows that this isn't a canon, but more of a club.

In practice, this canom is closed, so either the hub should be opened, or this should no longer be advertised as a canon.

I know a hub doesn't make a canon, a tag does, but the hub is still where most readers go (and expect) to find all the tales of that canon.

If a group of established authors with a high rated series written during a contest can't get onto the hub, what chance does any other writer have?
